facts.text: Spencertown grew from a 1756 deed by the Mohican Indians to a New England settlement, earning the nickname “land of contention” during colonial border disputes.
Peter’s Church, originally a 1771 meeting house, now houses the Austerlitz Town Hall after its 2019 relocation into the former Methodist Episcopal building.
The Austerlitz History Center, opened in a 1915 firehouse in Spencertown, displays the town’s story from Mohican times to the present.
Spencertown Academy, founded in 1847 as one of the first coeducational teacher‑training colleges, now serves as a community arts center hosting concerts and exhibitions.
Geographically, Spencertown sits at 686 feet above sea level in the Taconic foothills, where forest cover exceeds 60% and limestone soils support diverse hardwoods.
